## [alacritty](reference/alacritty.md)

Alacritty theme management: fetch the upstream theme pool and rewrite the `import` line in alacritty.toml, optionally picking day or night.

- [`alacritty_fetch_themes`](reference/alacritty.md#alacritty_fetch_themes) — Clone the upstream theme pool if missing, pull the latest themes, then list what is available.
- [`alacritty_is_night`](reference/alacritty.md#alacritty_is_night) — True when the local clock has passed the night threshold (ALACRITTY_NIGHT_HOUR, default 17).
- [`alacritty_list_themes`](reference/alacritty.md#alacritty_list_themes) — List the themes available in the local theme pool.
- [`alacritty_remove_themes`](reference/alacritty.md#alacritty_remove_themes) — Delete the local theme pool.
- [`alacritty_set_theme`](reference/alacritty.md#alacritty_set_theme) — Point alacritty.toml at a theme from the local pool.
- [`alacritty_setup`](reference/alacritty.md#alacritty_setup) — Fetch the theme pool and apply the time-of-day theme in one go.
- [`alacritty_update_themes`](reference/alacritty.md#alacritty_update_themes) — Pull the latest themes into the local pool.

## [cleanup](reference/cleanup.md)

macOS disk reclamation: estimate first, then purge caches by category behind an explicit confirmation. Merges the old `clean.sh` estimator with the unguarded cache removals that used to live in `ai.sh`.

- [`cleanup_all`](reference/cleanup.md#cleanup_all) — Run the full reclamation: print the estimate, then walk each category.
- [`cleanup_estimate`](reference/cleanup.md#cleanup_estimate) — Audit reclaimable disk space without deleting anything.
- [`cleanup_purge_ai`](reference/cleanup.md#cleanup_purge_ai) — Purge AI tooling caches: Hugging Face, Ollama, Claude Desktop's updater cache, and optionally the multi-gigabyte Claude VM bundle.
- [`cleanup_purge_apps`](reference/cleanup.md#cleanup_purge_apps) — Purge application and browser caches, plus the Homebrew download cache after running `brew cleanup`.
- [`cleanup_purge_dev`](reference/cleanup.md#cleanup_purge_dev) — Purge developer toolchain caches: uv, pip, go, npm, bun, swiftpm, Jedi, goimports, and the Python bytecode cache.
- [`cleanup_purge_hf`](reference/cleanup.md#cleanup_purge_hf) — Purge Hugging Face caches.
- [`cleanup_purge_vm`](reference/cleanup.md#cleanup_purge_vm) — Prune virtualization artefacts: unused Docker images, containers, networks and build cache, then Lima instance leftovers.

## [compat](reference/compat.md)

Cross-platform primitives. Modules MUST use these instead of calling xclip, pbcopy, xdg-open, `sed -i`, `readlink -f`, or `base64 -w` directly — those all differ between macOS (BSD) and Linux (GNU).

- [`b64_decode`](reference/compat.md#b64_decode) — Base64-decode stdin.
- [`b64_encode`](reference/compat.md#b64_encode) — Base64-encode stdin as a single line with no wrapping.
- [`clip_copy`](reference/compat.md#clip_copy) — Copy stdin to the system clipboard.
- [`clip_copy_file`](reference/compat.md#clip_copy_file) — Copy the contents of a file to the clipboard.
- [`clip_paste`](reference/compat.md#clip_paste) — Print the current system clipboard contents to stdout.
- [`gnu_sed`](reference/compat.md#gnu_sed) — Print the name of a GNU-compatible sed.
- [`os_open`](reference/compat.md#os_open) — Open a file, directory, or URL in the desktop default application.
- [`path_resolve`](reference/compat.md#path_resolve) — Resolve a path to its canonical absolute form, following symlinks.
- [`path_size`](reference/compat.md#path_size) — Print a human-readable size for a file or directory, or 0B if absent.
- [`sed_inplace`](reference/compat.md#sed_inplace) — Edit a file in place portably.
- [`timestamp`](reference/compat.md#timestamp) — Print an ISO-8601 timestamp suitable for filenames (no colons).
- [`tmp_dir`](reference/compat.md#tmp_dir) — Create a secure temporary directory and print its path.
- [`tmp_file`](reference/compat.md#tmp_file) — Create a secure temporary file and print its path.

## [docker-disk](reference/docker-disk.md)

Mount an external disk under Docker's data root and restore the iptables rules Docker needs afterwards. Linux only — this uses mount -t UUID=, iptables-restore, and systemd.

- [`docker_unmount_data_disk`](reference/docker-disk.md#docker_unmount_data_disk) — Stop docker and unmount the configured data disk.

## [media](reference/media.md)

ffmpeg video helpers: re-encode a file down to a sane size and report the before/after saving.

- [`media_shrink_video`](reference/media.md#media_shrink_video) — Re-encode a video to a smaller MP4 and report the size saved.

## [net](reference/net.md)

Network chores: public IP and ISP lookup, GitHub keys, URL scraping, media downloads, site mirroring, packet capture, and TLS issuance.

- [`net_copy_github_keys`](reference/net.md#net_copy_github_keys) — Copy someone's public SSH keys from GitHub to the clipboard, one key per line with their username appended as the comment.
- [`net_copy_ssh_pubkey`](reference/net.md#net_copy_ssh_pubkey) — Copy your own SSH public key to the clipboard.
- [`net_download_audio`](reference/net.md#net_download_audio) — Download audio only and transcode it to mp3.
- [`net_download_format`](reference/net.md#net_download_format) — Download a specific format id, as listed by net_list_formats.
- [`net_download_media`](reference/net.md#net_download_media) — Download a video with yt-dlp's defaults.
- [`net_download_video`](reference/net.md#net_download_video) — Download the best video and audio streams and merge them into mp4.
- [`net_dump_tcp_headers`](reference/net.md#net_dump_tcp_headers) — Dump readable ASCII payloads of TCP traffic heading to a port.
- [`net_extract_urls`](reference/net.md#net_extract_urls) — Print every absolute http(s) URL found on a page.
- [`net_extract_youtube_urls`](reference/net.md#net_extract_youtube_urls) — Print every YouTube watch URL found in the given files (or stdin).
- [`net_fetch_json`](reference/net.md#net_fetch_json) — Fetch a URL asking for JSON, following redirects.
- [`net_get_isp`](reference/net.md#net_get_isp) — Print the organisation (ISP) that owns this machine's public IP.
- [`net_get_movie_info`](reference/net.md#net_get_movie_info) — Look up a film or series on IMDb and print the JSON record.
- [`net_get_public_ip`](reference/net.md#net_get_public_ip) — Print this machine's public IPv4 address.
- [`net_issue_letsencrypt_cert`](reference/net.md#net_issue_letsencrypt_cert) — Issue a Let's Encrypt certificate using the manual DNS-01 challenge, in a throwaway working directory so nothing lands in /etc.
- [`net_list_formats`](reference/net.md#net_list_formats) — List every downloadable format for a URL, so you can pick an id.
- [`net_mirror_site`](reference/net.md#net_mirror_site) — Mirror a website for offline reading: recursive, page requisites, rewritten links, no walking above the starting path.
- [`net_normalize_ip`](reference/net.md#net_normalize_ip) — Turn a mangled IP such as AWS's `ip-10-0-3-17` or `10_0_3_17` back into a real dotted-quad, print it, and put it on the clipboard.
- [`net_open_github_user`](reference/net.md#net_open_github_user) — Open a GitHub user's profile in the browser.
- [`net_scan_hosts`](reference/net.md#net_scan_hosts) — Ping-sweep a network range and list the hosts that answer.

## [os](reference/os.md)

Operating system and package manager detection.

- [`is_linux`](reference/os.md#is_linux) — True when running on Linux.
- [`is_macos`](reference/os.md#is_macos) — True when running on macOS.
- [`os_arch`](reference/os.md#os_arch) — Print the CPU architecture normalised to arm64 or amd64.
- [`os_name`](reference/os.md#os_name) — Print the OS family as a lowercase token the loader uses for module directories: darwin, linux, or unknown.
- [`os_pkg_manager`](reference/os.md#os_pkg_manager) — Print the system package manager: brew, apt, pacman, dnf, or empty.
- [`pkg_install`](reference/os.md#pkg_install) — Install packages using whichever package manager this machine has.

## [pacman](reference/pacman.md)

Arch Linux package maintenance: orphan cleanup and cache pruning.

- [`pacman_clean_cache`](reference/pacman.md#pacman_clean_cache) — Prune old package versions from the pacman cache.
- [`pacman_list_orphans`](reference/pacman.md#pacman_list_orphans) — List packages that were pulled in as dependencies and are no longer required by anything.
- [`pacman_remove_orphans`](reference/pacman.md#pacman_remove_orphans) — Remove every orphaned package, along with its dependencies and configuration files.

## [process](reference/process.md)

Process inspection and control: what is holding a port, what is eating memory, and watching a command repeat.

- [`proc_kill_port`](reference/process.md#proc_kill_port) — Show which processes are listening on a TCP port, then kill them after an explicit confirmation.
- [`proc_top_memory`](reference/process.md#proc_top_memory) — List the processes with the highest resident memory share.
- [`proc_watch_command`](reference/process.md#proc_watch_command) — Re-run a command on an interval with changes highlighted.

## [procfs](reference/procfs.md)

Process inspection that reads /proc directly: environment of a live process, OOM killer scores, and thread counts.

- [`procfs_show_env`](reference/procfs.md#procfs_show_env) — Print the environment of a running process, one variable per line.
- [`procfs_show_passenger_threads`](reference/procfs.md#procfs_show_passenger_threads) — Print the thread count of every Phusion Passenger worker process.
- [`procfs_show_threads`](reference/procfs.md#procfs_show_threads) — Print the thread count of one or more processes.
- [`procfs_top_oom_scores`](reference/procfs.md#procfs_top_oom_scores) — List the processes most likely to be killed first when memory runs out, highest OOM score first, with their names.

## [prompt](reference/prompt.md)

Git-aware zsh prompt with abbreviated paths, plus AWS/Kubernetes context on the right and a cursor-shape vi-mode indicator.

- [`prompt_build_string`](reference/prompt.md#prompt_build_string) — Build the left-hand prompt string: failure marker, repo name, abbreviated path, branch and dirty marker.
- [`prompt_context_string`](reference/prompt.md#prompt_context_string) — Build the right-hand prompt: the active AWS profile and Kubernetes context.

## [shell](reference/shell.md)

Interactive shell baseline: locale, editor/pager, vi keybindings, unlimited shared history, and a few generic command helpers.

- [`shell_get_browser`](reference/shell.md#shell_get_browser) — Print the browser command this machine should use.
- [`shell_get_editor`](reference/shell.md#shell_get_editor) — Print the editor command this machine should use.
- [`shell_percol_history`](reference/shell.md#shell_percol_history) — Search shell history through percol and put the result on the command line.
- [`shell_reload`](reference/shell.md#shell_reload) — Re-source ~/.shellrc, picking up edits without opening a new shell.
- [`shell_retry`](reference/shell.md#shell_retry) — Re-run a command until it succeeds, at most N times (default: forever).
- [`shell_serve_http`](reference/shell.md#shell_serve_http) — Serve the current directory over HTTP.
- [`shell_setup_history`](reference/shell.md#shell_setup_history) — Configure effectively unlimited, timestamped, cross-session shell history for whichever shell is running.
- [`shell_time_command`](reference/shell.md#shell_time_command) — Time a command in whole seconds without needing bc or GNU date.

## [ssh](reference/ssh.md)

SSH config assembly from ~/.ssh/config.d, host listing, key generation, and EasySSH-driven inventory refresh.

- [`ssh_generate_host_config`](reference/ssh.md#ssh_generate_host_config) — Regenerate the ssh config fragment for one AWS account/region using easyssh, then rebuild ~/.ssh/config.
- [`ssh_generate_key`](reference/ssh.md#ssh_generate_key) — Generate a passphrase-less 4096-bit RSA keypair for an application under $SSH_KEYGEN_OUT_DIR (default ~/.ssh/generated, mode 700).
- [`ssh_generate_keys_all`](reference/ssh.md#ssh_generate_keys_all) — Generate a keypair for every name in $APPLICATION_LIST.
- [`ssh_list_hosts`](reference/ssh.md#ssh_list_hosts) — Print the Host names of production app/worker entries in ~/.ssh/config.
- [`ssh_list_hosts_matching`](reference/ssh.md#ssh_list_hosts_matching) — Print production hosts whose name matches a pattern.
- [`ssh_refresh_config`](reference/ssh.md#ssh_refresh_config) — Rebuild ~/.ssh/config from the fragments in $SSH_CONFIG_D.
- [`ssh_start_x2x`](reference/ssh.md#ssh_start_x2x) — Share this machine's keyboard and mouse with a remote X display over ssh, using x2x.

## [system](reference/system.md)

Linux-only machine maintenance: disk reclamation, package tarballs, webcam, and finding a Raspberry Pi on the LAN.

- [`system_enable_webcam`](reference/system.md#system_enable_webcam) — Load the USB video kernel module, for a webcam that did not come up.
- [`system_find_raspberry_pi`](reference/system.md#system_find_raspberry_pi) — Ping-sweep the LAN and print the addresses of any Raspberry Pi, matched on the Pi Foundation MAC prefixes.
- [`system_free_disk_space`](reference/system.md#system_free_disk_space) — Report reclaimable disk space, then optionally free it: package caches, Go module and build caches, yarn and yay caches, and the systemd journal.
- [`system_tarball_package`](reference/system.md#system_tarball_package) — Bundle every file an installed pacman package owns into a tarball, for copying onto a machine that cannot reach the repositories.
- [`system_test_webcam`](reference/system.md#system_test_webcam) — Show a live preview from the webcam, to check it works.

## [text](reference/text.md)

Text and string plumbing: base64, splitting, binary dumps, JSON pretty printing, QR codes, and .env file handling.

- [`text_copy_2fa_code`](reference/text.md#text_copy_2fa_code) — Pick a 2FA account with fzf and copy its current code to the clipboard.
- [`text_copy_and_announce`](reference/text.md#text_copy_and_announce) — Copy text to the clipboard and announce it with a talking cow.
- [`text_decode_base64`](reference/text.md#text_decode_base64) — Base64-decode arguments, or stdin when called with none.
- [`text_encode_base64`](reference/text.md#text_encode_base64) — Base64-encode arguments, or stdin when called with none.
- [`text_grep_env`](reference/text.md#text_grep_env) — Grep the environment case-insensitively.
- [`text_load_env_file`](reference/text.md#text_load_env_file) — Export every variable defined in a dotenv file.
- [`text_make_qrcode`](reference/text.md#text_make_qrcode) — Render text as a QR code directly in the terminal.
- [`text_pretty_json`](reference/text.md#text_pretty_json) — Pretty print JSON from a file or stdin.
- [`text_random_password`](reference/text.md#text_random_password) — Generate a random password of the given length.
- [`text_show_binary`](reference/text.md#text_show_binary) — Print the 8-bit binary representation of every character in the given text, one character per line.
- [`text_show_binary_inline`](reference/text.md#text_show_binary_inline) — Print the binary for some text as a single space-separated line, followed by the original text.
- [`text_split_lines`](reference/text.md#text_split_lines) — Split comma-separated values onto one line each.
- [`text_split_to_json_array`](reference/text.md#text_split_to_json_array) — Turn space-separated words into a JSON array of strings, ready to paste into a config file.
- [`text_unload_env_file`](reference/text.md#text_unload_env_file) — Unset every variable named in a dotenv file.

## [tls](reference/tls.md)

OpenSSL helpers: inspect a certificate file, inspect a live endpoint, and generate self-signed certificates for local testing.

- [`tls_gen_self_signed`](reference/tls.md#tls_gen_self_signed) — Generate a self-signed certificate, its key, and a concatenated PEM bundle (the form mongod and some proxies want) into a directory.
- [`tls_get_remote_info`](reference/tls.md#tls_get_remote_info) — Print the notBefore/notAfter dates of the certificate a TLS server is currently presenting.
- [`tls_show_cert`](reference/tls.md#tls_show_cert) — Print a certificate file in full human-readable form: subject, issuer, validity window, SANs, key usage, signature algorithm.
